audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option gives more weight to software, systems and algorithm design. The second applies computing and mathematics to signals, robotics and intelligent systems.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.text: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

DISARIN212.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
DISARIN212.text: Introduces formal logic, abstract reasoning and proof. Students work with propositions, quantified statements, sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, direct and indirect proofs, induction and recursion. A final component models processes and games without chance and investigates winning strategies.

DISARIN311.name: Optimization Methods in AI
DISARIN311.text: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.text: Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. DISDATA212.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
DISDATA212.text: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.
